candidate.answerReason: The five equal ratio parts each contain 6 students. Girls outnumber boys by one part.

methods.label: Use equal ratio parts
methods.explanation:
The ratio \(2:3\) represents \(2\) equal parts of boys and \(3\) equal parts of girls. Together these make \(2+3=5\) parts, so each part contains \(30\div5=6\) students.

There are therefore \(2\cdot6=12\) boys and \(3\cdot6=18\) girls. The girls outnumber the boys by \(18-12=\boxed{6}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
